chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
Nor is there a postponement (of payment) for his debt.
Nor is there charity given on his behalf.
Nor is there pilgrimage performed on his behalf.
Unless he had commanded that before his death.

key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: Charity given on behalf of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What acts of worship or financial obligations can be performed on behalf of a deceased person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify that posthumous actions like manumission or Hajj require explicit prior command, distinguishing them from the automatic deduction of debts and division of the estate. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the deceased's will is binding only for specific bequests, while general obligations are settled from the estate before inheritance distribution. The emphasis on explicit command protects the heirs' rights and ensures clarity in the execution of the deceased's final wishes.
